answer: Reciprocal escrow pairing. Each new identity must post an opal-denominated escrow that unlocks only after it completes a verified two-way transaction with an existing member, so the knoll of active identities grows one paid edge at a time. An attacker running N fakes needs N real counterparties paying real fees, since a fake-to-fake edge pays both sides' escrow penalties and yields nothing. The meadow of legitimate traders absorbs this cost cheaply because they transact anyway, while the attacker's per-identity cost scales with the number of genuine partners they must recruit and pay.
